description: JVM function values and wrappers slice (ISSUE-0098). JVM-only fixtures that run the real DEAL frontend (lexer → parser → name resolver → type checker) → real JvmBackend codegen → javac subprocess → java subprocess executing the emitted artifact (the harness fails a fixture whose codegen or JVM execution is bypassed). Covered forms: first-class function values in typed and inferred variables, indirect calls through variables/parameters/module fields and call-result callees, callbacks with primitive/string/null signatures, returning function values, the int/number conversion intrinsics as function values (exact and arity-extended), arity-extension adapters at variable-initializer and assignment positions — module functions and intrinsics delegate directly, module fields are read LIVE on every invoke (a reassignment after creation retargets the adapter, pinned cross-backend), and never-reassigned locals/parameters snapshot (reassigned bindings and non-identifier adapter values are E6000 until ISSUE-0110, pinned in JvmBackendTest) — E8010 runtime signature checks at callback and return boundaries with the checked value expression evaluated FIRST (evaluate-then-check side-effect order pinned cross-backend), wrapper reference equality, recursion routed through the wrapper, load-time indirect calls through function-typed module fields, and six frontend compile-error gates (E3001 parameter/return signature mismatch, E5004 reverse arity, E3009/E5001 indirect-call arity/argument mismatch, E3008 non-function callee) rejected before any backend. Eleven fixtures run under both backends as cross-backend parity with real luajit; two LuaJIT-only fixtures pin the reference semantics of the shapes the JVM slice conservatively rejects.

tests.name: jvm-fv-typed-variable-indirect-call
tests.description: First-class function value: a function declaration assigned to a typed variable of its exact signature and called indirectly through the variable (f(20, 22) = 42) — the call dispatches through the emitted wrapper's invoke, not a direct static call

tests.name: jvm-fv-inferred-variable
tests.description: Type inference for function values: `let f = dbl` infers the function type without an annotation and calls through the inferred wrapper (dbl(21) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-callback-param
tests.description: Callback through a function-typed parameter: apply(f: (int)=>int, v) calls its parameter indirectly (apply(inc, 41) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-callback-mixed-signatures
tests.description: Callback with a boolean/string signature: choose(f, true) calls the stored three-parameter function with boolean and string arguments and returns "jvm"

tests.name: jvm-fv-return-function-value
tests.description: Returning a function value: picker() returns the wrapped inc and the result is invoked immediately (picker()(41) = 42) — the callee is a call expression, dispatched through the returned wrapper

tests.name: jvm-fv-arity-extension-assign
tests.description: Arity extension at a variable initializer: (int)=>int assigned to an (int,int)=>int variable wraps the value in an adapter whose invoke accepts and silently ignores the extra parameter (f(41, 999) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-arity-extension-reassign
tests.description: Arity extension at an assignment: the wider function-typed variable is reassigned from the narrower function and the reassignment wraps the value in a fresh adapter (f = inc; f(41, 0) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-intrinsic-value-int
tests.description: The int conversion intrinsic as a first-class function value: ci: (number)=>int = int and ci(42.0) = 42 through the wrapper

tests.name: jvm-fv-intrinsic-value-number
tests.description: The number conversion intrinsic as a first-class function value: cn: (int)=>number = number and cn(42) = 42.0 through the wrapper

tests.name: jvm-fv-intrinsic-arity-extension
tests.description: Arity extension over an intrinsic value: (number)=>int assigned to a (number,string)=>int variable wraps int in an adapter whose invoke ignores the string (ci2(42.0, "ignored") = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-null-signatures
tests.description: Null in function signatures: () => null and (null) => int function values are stored, the void wrapper is invoked as a statement, and the null-parameter wrapper is called with null (wn(null) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-module-field-loadtime-call
tests.description: Module-level (load-time) indirect calls through function-typed module fields: the field holding the plain () => int wrapper, the field holding the arity-extension adapter, and the field holding the int intrinsic wrapper are all invoked inside the static initializer (42 + inc-adapter(41, 999) + int(40.0) = 124)

tests.name: jvm-fv-module-field-reassign-loadtime
tests.description: Module-level reassignment of a function-typed field before a load-time indirect call: the JVM static initializer mirrors LuaJIT's load-time execution, so the last assignment determines the held wrapper on both backends (f = dbl; f(2) = 4)

tests.name: jvm-fv-recursion-through-value
tests.description: Direct self-recursion routed through the function value: fact stores its own wrapper in a typed local and recurses through the indirect call (fact(5) = 120)

tests.name: jvm-fv-function-equality
tests.description: Function-value equality is wrapper reference identity: two reads of the same declaration's wrapper field compare equal (f === g with both holding inc), matching LuaJIT's wrapper-table identity

tests.name: jvm-fv-callback-chain
tests.description: A function value passed through a two-level callback chain: twice(inc, 20) applies the stored wrapper twice (20 + 1 + 1 = 22)

tests.name: jvm-fv-intrinsic-value-error
tests.description: A runtime error propagates through the intrinsic function-value wrapper: int(41.5) through the stored wrapper raises E8001 (non-integer number), exactly like the direct intrinsic call

tests.name: jvm-fv-sig-check-callback-error
tests.description: Signature check at a callback parameter boundary: passing (int)=>int where (int,string)=>int is declared compiles (arity extension) but raises E8010 at the parameter boundary when apply is entered, exactly like LuaJIT's wrapper check

tests.name: jvm-fv-sig-check-return-error
tests.description: Signature check at a return boundary: returning (int)=>int from a function declared (int,int)=>int compiles (arity extension) but raises E8010 when picker's return value crosses the declared boundary, exactly like LuaJIT's return check

tests.name: jvm-fv-frontend-sig-param-type
tests.description: Signature failure (parameter types): (string)=>int is not assignable to an (int)=>int variable — the frontend type checker rejects with E3001 before any backend runs

tests.name: jvm-fv-frontend-sig-return-type
tests.description: Signature failure (return type): () => string is not assignable to an () => int variable — E3001 before any backend runs

tests.name: jvm-fv-frontend-sig-reverse-arity
tests.description: Signature failure (reverse arity): (int)=>int is not assignable to an () => int variable (actual has MORE parameters than the target) — the frontend rejects with the dedicated E5004 reverse-arity diagnostic before any backend runs

tests.name: jvm-fv-frontend-indirect-arity
tests.description: Indirect-call arity failure: calling a one-parameter function value with two arguments is E3009 before any backend runs

tests.name: jvm-fv-frontend-indirect-arg-type
tests.description: Indirect-call argument-type failure: a string argument to a one-int-parameter function value is E5001 before any backend runs

tests.name: jvm-fv-frontend-call-non-function
tests.description: Calling a non-function value: an int variable used as a callee is E3008 ("int is not callable") before any backend runs

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-callback-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): the callback apply(inc, 41) = 42 shape runs through both backends' real codegen and execution and prints the same marker

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-arity-assign-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): the arity-extension assignment adapter ignores the extra parameter on both backends (f(41, 999) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-intrinsic-value-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): the int intrinsic stored as a function value converts through the wrapper on both backends (ci(42.0) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-reassignment-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): reassigning a function-typed variable retargets later calls on both backends (f = dbl; f(21) = 42)

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-boolean-boundary-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): an indirect call through an inferred function-typed variable applies the same typed boolean boundary as a direct call — a past-end boolean[] read's nil passed through && as the boolean argument fails the parameter boundary with E8001, exit 1 on both backends (the JVM converts the boxed temporary with booleanNotNull at the argument position: E8001 "expected boolean, got null"; LuaJIT's check_boolean(nil) at callee entry).

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-field-adapter-reassign-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): an arity-extension adapter over a function-typed MODULE FIELD reads the binding live on every invoke on both backends, so reassigning the field after the adapter's creation retargets the adapter (g = dbl; h(10, 999) = 20 — never a stale 11)

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-loadtime-field-adapter-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): the load-time variant — a module-level adapter over a function-typed module field is created in the static initializer, the field is reassigned at load, and the adapter's later invoke reads the field live on both backends (h(10, 999) = 20)

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-e8010-callback-eval-order
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): at an E8010 callback-parameter check position the argument value expression is evaluated before the check raises — the marker prints only when markF("pre", inc) ran before markI("post", 1) (spec §Operational semantics rule 2), and the E8010 still follows on both backends (exit 1)

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-e8010-return-eval
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): at an E8010 return-boundary check position the returned value expression is evaluated before the check raises — markF logs its marker and only then does the E8010 fire on both backends (exit 1); the pre-fix JVM dropped the side effect entirely

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-callee-eval-order-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): a call-result callee evaluates COMPLETELY before any argument (spec §Operational semantics rule 1) even when a later argument hoists side-effecting pre-statements — picker() runs first and its past-end int[] read raises E8001 before bump()'s negative-index E8002 or the && operand's hoisted read can run, exit 1 on both backends (the pre-fix JVM hoisted bump()'s read first and raised E8002; 'negative array index' is pinned never to appear)

tests.name: jvm-fv-cross-callee-e8010-order-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity (LuaJIT + JVM): a call-result callee whose return boundary raises E8010 (picker returns (int)=>int where (int,boolean)=>int is declared) evaluates and raises BEFORE any argument — the hoisted bump() negative-index read and the && operand never run, so only E8010 appears and 'negative array index' never prints, exit 1 on both backends (the pre-fix JVM hoisted bump()'s read first and raised E8002)

tests.name: jvm-fv-lua-ref-reassigned-adapter
tests.description: LuaJIT reference semantics for the reassigned-local adapter shape that the JVM slice conservatively rejects with E6000 (pinned in JvmBackendTest.testFunctionValues): LuaJIT's adapter reads the binding live on every invoke, so f = dbl retargets the earlier adapter (h(10, 999) = 20)

tests.name: jvm-fv-lua-ref-callresult-adapter
tests.description: LuaJIT reference semantics for the side-effecting call-result adapter shape that the JVM slice conservatively rejects with E6000 (pinned in JvmBackendTest.testFunctionValues): LuaJIT's adapter re-evaluates picker() on EVERY invoke — two invokes run picker twice (count reaches 2), so 33 + 33 + 2 = 68; a creation-time-only evaluation would compute 67
